title: Queue order by an account's share and the daily cap (the founder's Q7 of 2026-10-21)
assertion: Every upload accepted; an account's k-th upload past its 100,000-row share of the UTC day waits at priority -k (at most -20), and an upload past the day's 1,000,000-row cap of normal-tier rows at -1; the account kept only as the rate limiter's keyed subject; the cap counts the normal tier only; both sums read an append-only tally of the day's uploads, so an upload a later screening of the same practice or address replaced still counts (one mailbox resubmitting 50,000-row files gets 0, 0, -1, -2), the tally granted to no role and purged after the next UTC day; the waiting tier on a queue of its own, worked with one thread fewer than the consumer has, so a normal upload never waits behind waiting-tier runs holding every thread; a sweep fails a run out of attempts only while it is still stale under its lock; the due runs, the queue gauge and the wait ordered by priority, then age; a waiting run's time to email logged apart from the promise's metric; no upload of the capacity test waits
noFileReason: The tiers come from uploads the tests submit in memory under synthetic accounts; no file.
